summary: The diff implements Iterator.prototype.windows in its own file and follows the spec steps in order. Steps 1-7 validate this, the ? and IteratorClose error paths are correct, and GetIteratorDirect is called at step 8. The closure matches steps 9.a-9.b: IteratorStepValue with ? propagation, the partial-window yield when allow-partial applies, the sliding buffer, and IfAbruptCloseIterator on a return at a full-window yield. The partial-yield resume is handled by a flag, so a return there is discarded as step 9.b.ii.1.a requires. Buffer values are traced for GC. No test-shaped branches, no swallowed errors, no fabricated values. Nothing in the diff is unrelated to the ticket; the only other change is renaming an unused parameter to _new_target. Remaining uncertainty is in framework code I cannot see: how the helper treats a return, and whether iterator_close_all(Ok) performs the step 7 object check.
notes_for_next_attempt: No defects found. Optional cleanup: the undersized check allocates a Vec<u16> on every comparison and could compare the code units against a static slice. Before merging, confirm that HelperClosure's generic return path does not close the underlying iterator a second time, and that iterator_close_all(agent, underlying, Ok(())) performs the step 7 "not an Object" TypeError check.
